production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): its 2016 570S page and year selector list 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020, and its 2021 address redirects to the 2020 page, "Used 2020 McLaren 570S" (kbb-570s-2020). KBB calls the 2016 car "an all-new model". McLaren's US press kit of October 2015 (mclaren-us-570s-press-kit-2015) gives "deliveries in the U.S. starting before the end of 2015" but no model year. No McLaren page was found that names the first or last US model year.

body.note: "570S Coupe", a two-seat fixed-roof car. The 570S Spider and the 570GT are sold under their own names and are not part of this record.

displacementL.note: 3,799 cc ("Engine configuration V8 Twin Turbo / 3,799cc"); McLaren calls it a "3.8-liter twin turbo V8".

aspiration.note: "V8 Twin Turbo"; "3.8-liter twin turbo V8 engine"

drivetrain.note: McLaren US press kit: "The classic mid-engine rear-wheel drive supercar configuration optimizes handling and agility."

transmission.note: "Transmission 7 Speed SSG" (McLaren "seven-speed seamless shift gearbox"), recorded as a DCT as in the McLaren 720S record, where McLaren describes its SSG as "A dual-clutch, seamless-shift gearbox". No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (McLaren US press kit, October 2015): "Power 562 hp (570PS) @ 7,400 rpm". The global kit of October 2015 (mclaren-570s-press-kit-2015) has "Power 570PS (562 bhp) @ 7,400 rpm"; McLaren's May 2016 Sports Series kit (mclaren-sports-series-press-kit-2016) gives "Power 570PS (562 bhp) @ 7,500 rpm" (same output, different peak rpm). powerStandard is DIN PS because McLaren's rating is the metric 570 PS; 570 x 0.98632 = 562 hp, the figure McLaren's US kit prints.

weightLb.note: Dry weight of a car with lightweight options (guide step 4), coupe with the 7-speed SSG (the only transmission). Quote (McLaren US press kit): "Dry weight 2,895 lbs (1,313 kg) with lightweight options"; the global kits (mclaren-570s-press-kit-2015, mclaren-sports-series-press-kit-2016) give "Dry weight 1,313 kg (2,895 lb) with lightweight options". McLaren does not name the options. A standard car is heavier, and a car with fluids heavier still. No McLaren kerb weight for the standard or an optioned 570S Coupe was found (steps 1 and 3), and no qualifying publication curb weight (step 2). McLaren's 600LT US media pack (mclaren-us-600lt-media-pack-2018) says the 600LT is "220.5lbs lighter* than 570S Coupe DIN kerbweight", but a 570S kerb weight worked out from that by subtraction is not used. That pack shows McLaren did publish a 570S Coupé DIN kerb weight somewhere; it was not found, and would replace this figure if it is.
